metaTitle: Where Do Cockroaches Come From? The 4 Ways In
metaDescription: Cockroaches are carried in with boxes and furniture, cross shared walls, come up floor drains or walk in from the yard. Match the species to its route.
h1: Where Do Cockroaches Come From? The Four Ways They Get Into a Home
dek: The four routes cockroaches use to get indoors, which species uses which, why a clean house is not protected, and the specific fix that closes each one.
excerpt: Cockroaches are carried in, cross shared apartment walls, come up from drains or walk in from the yard. Which species uses which route, and how to close it.

quickAnswer.lead: **Cockroaches reach a home by four routes: carried in with boxes, bags, furniture and appliances; through shared walls and plumbing from a neighboring unit; up through floor drains from the sewer; or in from the yard through gaps around doors, vents and the roofline.** The species tells you which route to check, and the [University of Kentucky's cockroach fact sheet](https://entomology.mgcafe.uky.edu/ef614) notes that even clean homes can become infested.
bullets: German cockroaches, about 1/2 inch long, spend their lives indoors, so they arrive in groceries, boxes, furniture and appliances or from an adjoining unit.
American cockroaches, 1.5 to 2 inches long, live in sewers, where more than 5,000 have been found in a single manhole, and come up through floor drains and plumbing.
Oriental cockroaches, 1 to 1.25 inches long, come in under doors, along pipes from the crawl space and through floor drains, and usually stay at or below ground level.
Smokybrown and wood cockroaches live outdoors in mulch, tree holes and woodpiles and get in through roof soffits, door gaps and firewood.
An adult German cockroach can hide in a crack 1/16 inch wide, which is why sealing around pipes and doors is part of every fix.
A gravel strip 6 to 12 inches wide around the building is one of the yard changes the University of California suggests.

body.text: How do cockroaches get into a house?

Cockroaches get in by four routes: inside things people carry in, through the walls and plumbing of a shared building, up from the sewer through drains, and in from outdoors through gaps in the shell of the house. [Texas A&M AgriLife Extension](https://mytexas.ag.tamu.edu/publications/cockroach-biology-and-management/) covers the first two in one sentence: cockroaches can infest a home when they are brought in with groceries or boxes and, once established, readily move within a structure, for example from apartment to apartment. It adds that the larger species, such as American and smokybrown cockroaches, often enter through poorly sealed doors, roof soffits (the underside of the roof overhang) or floor drains.

Which route applies depends on the species. Texas A&M says German cockroaches spend their lives indoors, so one in your kitchen did not wander in from the garden. A wood cockroach is the reverse: the University of Kentucky says it lives outdoors under loose bark and cannot survive inside a house. Identify the insect first, using [the main cockroach species found in US homes](/learn/cockroaches) if you are unsure, then check the route that species uses.

body.text: The size ranges reflect small differences between fact sheets. The [University of California's cockroach guide](https://ipm.ucanr.edu/home-and-landscape/cockroaches/) (UC IPM) lists the American cockroach at 2 inches where Kentucky and the University of Florida give about 1.5 inches, and it lists the Oriental cockroach at 1.25 inches where Kentucky and Penn State say about 1 inch. If your insect matches none of these rows, it may not be a cockroach at all: compare it with [the beetles, crickets and other insects most often mistaken for cockroaches](/blog/bugs-that-look-like-cockroaches).

body.text: How do cockroaches get carried into a home?

They ride in hidden inside things that came from an infested place. The University of Kentucky says the German cockroach is often introduced in infested grocery bags, beverage cartons or furniture, and UC IPM tells readers to look for entry on items brought into the building, especially appliances, furniture, boxes and anything that was recently in storage.

The German cockroach is the species this route explains best, because an insect that spends its life indoors is not walking in from the yard. UC IPM calls it the most common indoor cockroach in California and perhaps worldwide, especially in multi-unit housing, and says an adult can hide in a crack just 1/16 inch wide. An insect that small and flat is easy to miss in the folds of a carton or the housing of a used appliance. A separate guide explains [how to recognize a German cockroach and why a few arrivals multiply so fast](/blog/german-cockroaches).

Other species hitchhike too. [Penn State Extension](https://extension.psu.edu/oriental-cockroaches) notes that Oriental cockroaches may enter a home in food packages and laundry, and Kentucky says wood cockroaches are brought in during winter in firewood. The brownbanded cockroach, another indoor species about 1/2 inch long, hides in and near electrical appliances, behind wall decorations and inside hollow furniture legs, according to UC IPM. That page does not describe how brownbanded cockroaches arrive, but those hiding places are the same items it says to check.
How to close the carried-in route

items: **Look before you carry it in.** Check secondhand appliances and furniture, and anything coming out of storage, before it enters the house, paying attention to crevices, hollow legs and appliance housings.

**Unpack and clear the packaging.** Grocery bags, beverage cartons and boxes are the carriers the extension sources name, so empty them promptly. UC IPM also says to remove piles of paper bags, boxes and newspapers, which give cockroaches places to hide.

**Treat firewood as an outdoor item.** UC IPM advises removing stacks of lumber or firewood from around the outside of buildings, and a practical response to Kentucky's point about winter firewood is to bring in only the logs you are about to burn.

**Set sticky traps after a move or a secondhand purchase.** UC IPM calls sticky traps the best way to detect and monitor cockroaches, and a related guide explains [what glue traps can tell you and what they cannot do](/blog/best-roach-traps-canada).

body.text: How do cockroaches spread between apartments?

They walk through the building itself, along pipes and wires and through gaps in shared walls, floors and ceilings. Kentucky states that in multi-unit dwellings such as apartments, cockroaches travel between units through common walls and ceilings, and Texas A&M describes them moving readily from apartment to apartment once they are established.

A [study of a 188-unit high-rise in Paterson, New Jersey](https://academic.oup.com/jee/article/112/5/2302/5491551), published in the Journal of Economic Entomology in 2019, mapped what that looks like. Before treatment, German cockroach infestations in the building were spatially correlated: apartments that shared a wall, faced each other across the hallway or sat directly above and below one another tended to share the same infestation status. After 12 months of building-wide integrated pest management, only the correlation between floors remained, and the authors concluded that such a program reduces cockroach movement between units as well as clearing individual apartments.

For a tenant, that means roaches in a spotless apartment may have come from next door, and that treating one unit alone can leave the source in place. Report them to the property manager and ask whether the adjoining units will be inspected. On your side of the wall, Kentucky recommends sealing the openings where plumbing pipes or wires pass through walls or floors with caulk, foam or copper mesh, and says this is especially useful in apartments for reducing migration between adjoining units. Texas A&M adds the gaps around sinks and plumbing and along kitchen splash guards.
Do cockroaches really come up through drains?

Yes. American and Oriental cockroaches use floor drains as common points of entry into buildings, according to Texas A&M, and both live in the sewers those drains connect to. The [University of Florida's American cockroach profile](https://ask.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/IN298) says the species is found mainly in basements, sewers, steam tunnels and drainage systems, that more than 5,000 have sometimes been found in a single sewer manhole, and that they migrate into houses and apartments from sewers by way of the plumbing.

What normally stops them is water. Texas A&M's advice is to keep P-traps, the U-shaped bends in drain pipes, filled with water to create a barrier between the sewer and the home. UC IPM describes the failures: American cockroaches occasionally forage from sewers into the ground floor of buildings, especially if pipes are damaged, screens are missing or the water traps in drains are faulty. A trap only works while it holds water, so a rarely used floor drain in a basement, laundry room or garage deserves a look and a top-up with water if it has gone dry.

body.text: Oriental cockroaches use the plumbing in a second way. Penn State says they frequently move into a home along the pipes, for example up through the floor from the crawl space underneath, and that indoors they are usually at or below ground level and seldom on walls, in high cupboards or on upper floors. UC IPM adds that they cannot climb smooth vertical surfaces and may be found trapped in porcelain sinks or tubs after falling in or after climbing up through damaged drain pipes, so a roach in the bathtub is not proof that it came up the drain. UC IPM also notes that this species is sometimes called a water bug, a name sorted out in [how a true water bug differs from a cockroach](/blog/water-bugs-vs-cockroaches).

Weather pushes both species indoors. The University of Florida says American cockroaches are rarely found in houses but that infestations can occur after heavy rain, and Penn State reports considerable movement of Oriental cockroaches into structures during drought, apparently in search of higher humidity.
Which cockroaches come in from outdoors?

American, Oriental, smokybrown, wood and field cockroaches all live outdoors and can come inside. Texas A&M says the first three live mostly outdoors but may move indoors in search of food or water, and Kentucky names the openings that American, Oriental and wood cockroaches use: gaps around windows, doors, vents and utility openings.

items: **American.** The University of Florida says that outdoors it is found in moist, shady places such as hollow trees, woodpiles and mulch, that it moves into buildings from trees and shrubs growing alongside them or with branches overhanging the roof, and that it is occasionally found under roof shingles and in attics.

**Oriental.** Penn State finds it outdoors in warm weather beneath leaves, in bark mulch around shrubs and foundations, in stone walls and in water valve pits, and says it comes in under doors and through air ducts, garbage chutes and ventilators. UC IPM adds that it is common where people feed pets, livestock or wildlife outside.

**Smokybrown.** Texas A&M describes it as common outdoors in the more humid parts of Texas and other southern states, living in ground cover, mulch, palm fronds, tree holes, soffits and attic eaves. UC IPM says it sometimes invades homes and takes refuge in the attic.
**Wood cockroaches.** Kentucky describes large numbers wandering in from outside during spring and summer and notes that they are attracted to lights.

**Field cockroach.** UC IPM says this small striped species, often mistaken for the German cockroach, may invade indoor areas when it is hot or dry outside and is most common in southern California and desert areas.

**Turkestan.** Texas A&M says this introduced species is expanding its range into Texas, and both it and UC IPM place it outdoors in water meter boxes, compost, leaf litter and potted plants. Neither fact sheet describes a typical route indoors.

body.text: Several of these species fly, which changes where the gap is likely to be. Texas A&M says adult American cockroaches of both sexes can fly, though Kentucky notes that they seldom do; UC IPM says smokybrown adults fly, especially on warm, humid evenings; and Kentucky calls male wood cockroaches excellent fliers. A large roach in an attic or an upstairs room in the South is a reason to check the roofline, where Texas A&M says soffits should be screened, and not only the doors and foundation. A sibling guide covers [which cockroaches fly and which only glide](/blog/can-cockroaches-fly).

An outdoor roach indoors is not always the start of an infestation. Kentucky says wood cockroaches cannot survive indoors, so one that wandered in is a nuisance and nothing more. American and Oriental cockroaches are different: Kentucky places both in the dark, moist parts of buildings, including basements, crawl spaces and cellars.
Why do clean homes still get cockroaches?

Because none of the four routes depends on housekeeping. After listing the ways cockroaches are introduced, Kentucky concludes that roaches usually thrive where sanitation is poor but that even clean homes can become infested. A German cockroach in a grocery bag, a sewer roach under a dry floor drain and a neighbor's infestation on the other side of a shared wall all reach a spotless kitchen as easily as a dirty one.

Cleanliness decides what happens next. UC IPM says cockroaches thrive where they can find food, water and shelter, and that even tiny amounts of crumbs or liquids caught between cracks provide a food source. Its figures also show why the species matters: a single female German cockroach and her offspring can produce over 30,000 individuals in a year, compared with over 800 for an American cockroach and nearly 200 for an Oriental. Food stored in insect-proof containers, trash kept under tight-fitting lids and repaired plumbing leaks, all on UC IPM's list, will not stop a roach from arriving, but they make it harder for a few arrivals to become a population.

There is a health reason to close the routes as well. UC IPM reports that indoor cockroach infestations are important sources of allergens and have been identified as risk factors for the development of asthma in children. If anyone in the home has asthma or allergy symptoms that are worse indoors, tell their healthcare provider about the roaches. Whether the insects also bite is a separate question, answered in [what is actually documented about cockroach bites](/blog/do-cockroaches-bite).
How do you close each route?

Match the fix to the route your species uses, and start with exclusion. UC IPM states that pesticides alone will not solve a cockroach problem and calls limiting the avenues of access to living areas an essential part of managing them.

body.caption: Each step follows from the extension fact sheets linked on this page; the drain-repair and branch-trimming steps answer entry conditions those sources describe.

body.text: The yard steps work by removing shelter and moisture next to the walls: UC IPM recommends trimming shrubbery to increase light and air circulation, especially near vents, and the University of Florida says that limiting moist areas in and around a structure reduces what attracts American cockroaches.

body.title: Sealing keeps roaches out; it does not remove the ones inside
body.text: Exclusion stops new arrivals. A population that is already breeding indoors needs monitoring and treatment as well, and any pesticide used must be applied exactly as its label directs.
For an established indoor population, the next step is [a bait-first plan for getting rid of cockroaches](/blog/how-to-get-rid-of-cockroaches-canada).
Is it one stray or an infestation?

The species tells you most of it, and traps tell you the rest. A single large roach on a ground floor after heavy rain or during a dry spell, or a wood cockroach in spring, fits the pattern of a stray from outside. A German cockroach is another matter. Because the species spends its life indoors, one in a kitchen came from a population somewhere in the building or from something recently carried in.

To check, set sticky traps where floors meet walls and close to where you suspect activity, which is where UC IPM says to place them. Kentucky notes that cockroaches are more active at night and spend the day hidden in cracks and other dark, secluded areas, so traps see what you do not. If they catch small wingless nymphs as well as adults, that is a sign the roaches are reproducing close by; a companion guide shows [what baby cockroaches of each species look like](/blog/what-do-baby-cockroaches-look-like). Where the catch is highest also points to the route: beside a floor drain, along the wall shared with a neighbor, or next to an exterior door.

If traps keep catching German cockroaches, or sewer roaches keep appearing despite full traps and sealed gaps, the source is probably outside your reach: a neighboring unit, a damaged sewer line or a crawl space. That is the point to involve the property manager, a plumber or a pest control company, and [what professional pest control typically costs](/blog/how-much-is-pest-control) gives a sense of the budget.

faqs.question: Does seeing one cockroach mean there are more?
faqs.answer: It depends on the species. Texas A&M AgriLife Extension says German cockroaches spend their lives indoors, so a single one in a kitchen or bathroom came from a population in the building or from something carried in, and the University of Kentucky notes that cockroaches stay hidden in cracks during the day. A large outdoor species such as an American, Oriental or wood cockroach can be a lone stray that came in through a gap. Sticky traps set where floors meet walls will show which situation you have.

faqs.question: Can cockroaches come up through a sink or bathtub drain?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but floor drains are the entry point the extension sources call common. Texas A&M AgriLife Extension says American and Oriental cockroaches use floor drains to enter buildings and advises keeping the P-traps filled with water, which forms a barrier between the sewer and the home. For sinks and tubs, UC IPM says Oriental cockroaches cannot climb smooth vertical surfaces and may be found trapped in porcelain sinks or tubs after falling in or after climbing up through damaged drain pipes. A roach in the tub may therefore have come up a damaged drain line, or it may simply have fallen in and been unable to climb out.

faqs.question: Where do cockroaches come from in an apartment?
faqs.answer: Usually from a neighboring unit or from something carried in. The University of Kentucky says cockroaches in multi-unit buildings travel between units through common walls and ceilings, and a 2019 study of a 188-unit high-rise in Paterson, New Jersey, found that infested apartments were clustered with infested neighbors before a building-wide program began. Kentucky recommends sealing the openings where pipes and wires pass through walls and floors with caulk, foam or copper mesh. Report the problem to the property manager, because treating one unit alone can leave the source in place.

faqs.question: What attracts cockroaches to a house?
faqs.answer: Food, water and shelter. UC IPM says cockroaches thrive wherever they find all three and that even tiny amounts of crumbs or liquids caught between cracks are a food source, so leaks, open trash and unsealed food all help a population grow. Outdoors, UC IPM notes that Oriental cockroaches are common where people feed pets, livestock or wildlife, and it recommends removing dense ground cover and stacks of lumber or firewood from beside the building. The University of Kentucky adds that wood cockroaches are attracted to lights.

faqs.question: What time of year do cockroaches come inside?
faqs.answer: It varies by species. German cockroaches live indoors all year. Penn State Extension says Oriental cockroaches are generally outdoors in warm weather and move into structures during drought, and the University of Florida says American cockroach infestations in houses can follow heavy rain. The University of Kentucky describes wood cockroaches wandering in during spring and summer and arriving in firewood in winter. UC IPM says the field cockroach may come indoors when it is hot or dry outside. Drought, heat and heavy rain are among the triggers these sources name for the outdoor species.

faqs.question: Where do cockroaches hide during the day?
faqs.answer: In dark, tight spaces close to food and water. The University of Kentucky says cockroaches are more active at night and generally spend the day hidden in cracks and other dark, secluded areas. UC IPM lists typical daytime hiding places as around water heaters, in cupboard cracks, in stoves, in crawl spaces and in outdoor vegetation, and says they move into kitchens and other areas at night. It also notes that false-bottom cupboards and hollow walls are common refuges that should be sealed.
